content:
Date: Sunday, June 28, 2026

Selected Approach:
- Pin one npm version across all three environments (sandbox, CI, local)

Approved implementation approach:
Add "packageManager": "npm@10.9.7" to package.json (Corepack-enforced — the node-22 default npm), enable Corepack locally, and update verify.yml + auto-pr.yml to pin/enable the same npm before npm ci (e.g. corepack enable or npm i -g npm@10.9.7). Then regenerate both lockfiles once so they're emitted by the pinned version. This targets the root cause: identical npm everywhere → identical os/cpu/libc emission everywhere.

Andrew's Answers:
Q: Both lockfiles in scope? The churn affects frontend/package-lock.json (266 platform-field lines) and the root ./package-lock.json (16). My plan is to fix both so neither churns — flag if you'd rather scope it to just frontend/ for now. Optional
  A (Andrew confirmed your prediction): Yes — fix both frontend/package-lock.json and the root ./package-lock.json so neither churns.
Q: OK to pin the npm version in CI? The load-bearing half of the recommended fix is standardizing on one npm version (the node-22 default, npm@10.9.7) and updating verify.yml + auto-pr.yml to use it — otherwise CI keeps re-emitting different fields. Confirm editing the workflows is fine, and that 10.9.7 is the version to standardize on (or name your local npm if it differs). Optional
  A (Andrew confirmed your prediction): Yes — pin npm@10.9.7 (node-22 default) and update both workflows to use it; that matches what I run locally.

Proceed with implementation.
